source: Publisher documentation saved under e3/truth/docs/fresh/ (sha256 in SHA256SUMS): TPC-DS v3.2.0; LDBC SNB specification (v2.2.5-SNAPSHOT, Appendix D for the Interactive v1 legacy data sets); GTFS Schedule Reference; FAA ardata.pdf (5/8/2025); ABS ASGS Edition 3 web pages; SEC Financial Statement Data Sets; College Scorecard Field of Study documentation (October 2026) and data dictionary; EPA AirData FileFormats (v3.0.0); 2024 ACS PUMS data dictionary and Census regions and divisions; City of Chicago portal metadata (ijzp-q8t2, c7ck-438e); USDA FoodData Central download field descriptions (October 2020)
rule: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or nesting statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened.

instance.generator: public data fixed before download for the confirmatory evaluation, joined by fresh.py
instance.construction: SEC Financial Statement Data Sets, quarter 2026Q3 (2026q3.zip): NUM (root, sampled to 1,000,000 records if larger) left-joined to SUB on adsh and to TAG on (tag, version); empty segments and coreg are the value '?'; dropped NUM footnote and TAG doc (free text), TAG abstract (0 for every tag of a numeric fact in NUM), and the address, phone, incorporation, former-name, filing-status and file-name columns of SUB to stay within 25 columns.

cleaning.missing_values: empty and missing references become '?', kept as a value (null = null)

truth.clause: sec_financial-statement-data-sets.pdf, 3 Organization (pp. 2-3): "NUM is a data set of all numeric XBRL facts presented on the primary financial statements as rendered by the Comission. A unique key of each row is a combination of the following fields:" (adsh, tag, version, ddate, qtrs, uom, segments, coreg); sec_financial-statement-data-sets.pdf, 5 Table Definitions (p. 4): "the column is a function of all or some of a unique key."
truth.justification: The eight fields are the declared unique key of NUM, and value is a non-key column of NUM; empty segments and coreg are kept as the value '?'.

audit.quote: "NUM is a data set of all numeric XBRL facts presented on the primary financial statements as rendered by the Comission. A unique key of each row is a combination of the following fields:" (adsh, tag, version, ddate, qtrs, uom, segments, coreg) (3 Organization, pp. 2-3); "the column is a function of all or some of a unique key." (5 Table Definitions, p. 4)

truth.clause: sec_financial-statement-data-sets.pdf, 3 Organization (p. 2): "SUB identifies all the EDGAR submissions with amounts rendered by the Commission on the primary financial statements in the data set, with each row having the unique (primary) key adsh"; (p. 3): "The Accession Number (adsh) found in the NUM data set can be used to retrieve information about the submission in SUB."; sec_financial-statement-data-sets.pdf, 5 Table Definitions (p. 4): "the column is a function of all or some of a unique key."
truth.justification: adsh is the primary key of SUB, referenced from NUM; name and sic are 'as of the filing date', so cik does not determine them across submissions.

audit.quote: "SUB identifies all the EDGAR submissions with amounts rendered by the Commission on the primary financial statements in the data set, with each row having the unique (primary) key adsh" (p. 2); "The Accession Number (adsh) found in the NUM data set can be used to retrieve information about the submission in SUB." (p. 3); "the column is a function of all or some of a unique key." (5 Table Definitions, p. 4)

A unique key of each row is a combination of these fields:" (tag, version); (p. 3): "Information about the tag used can be found in TAG."; sec_financial-statement-data-sets.pdf, 5 Table Definitions (p. 4): "the column is a function of all or some of a unique key."
truth.justification: (tag, version) is the declared unique key of TAG, referenced from NUM.

audit.quote: "TAG is a data set of all numerical tags used in the submissions, both standard and custom. A unique key of each row is a combination of these fields:" (tag, version) (p. 2); "Information about the tag used can be found in TAG." (p. 3); "the column is a function of all or some of a unique key." (5 Table Definitions, p. 4)

truth.clause: sec_financial-statement-data-sets.pdf, 5.2 TAG (p. 7): "custom 1 if tag is custom (version=adsh), 0 if it is standard. Note: This flag is technically redundant with the version and adsh columns."
truth.justification: The documentation states that custom is redundant with version and adsh (custom = 1 exactly when version equals the accession number).

audit.quote: "1 if tag is custom (version=adsh), 0 if it is standard. Note: This flag is technically redundant with the version and adsh columns." (5.2 TAG, Figure 3, p. 7)

truth.clause: sec_financial-statement-data-sets.pdf, 5.2 TAG (p. 7): "For a standard tag, an identifier for the taxonomy; otherwise the accession number where the tag was defined."
truth.justification: A version value is either a taxonomy identifier (custom = 0) or an accession number (custom = 1), so it determines custom if the two kinds of value never coincide, which is not stated; unsure.

audit.quote: "For a standard tag, an identifier for the taxonomy; otherwise the accession number where the tag was defined." (5.2 TAG, p. 7)

gold_design_note: No normalized design is published; the 3NF designs of Sigma* are synthesized.

mined.algorithm: fdmine.py: exact discovery of all minimal FDs in the style of HyFD (no HyFD binary was available); the complete set of minimal FDs is unique, so it equals HyFD's output
